newsitem.title: UK: UK's OFWAT to set water leakage targets for '98/99.
newsitem.headline: UK's OFWAT to set water leakage targets for '98/99.

text.p: UK regulator OFWAT on Monday said in a statement it was keeping up pressure on water companies to reduce leakage by setting demanding mandatory targets for 1998/99.
These build on the targets already in place for 1997/98.

The current targets aims to reduce leakages by 150 million gallons a day, or by around 15 percent from the most recent figures for 1995/96. Details of performance in 1996/97 will be published in the autumn.
"Companies must realise that the regulator and the new government want to see leakage tackled more vigorously," Ian Byatt, Director General of Water Services told the government's water summit today.

"Some companies have been getting on with leakage reduction; in other case I have taken regulatory action to ensure progress is made -- for instance Thames (Water Plc) is now reporting its leakage to me quarterly," he added.
Byatt said targets are needed to ensure progress is made and that "enforcement action" will be taken against companies if he is not satisfied.

Byatt said the targets for 1998/99 will be set and published in the autumn. The targets will focus on total leakage from both company and customers' pipes and should reduce overall leakage "substantially below present levels".
The companies are expected to help customers by offering free or subsidised repairs to customer leaking pipes.
It is the intention to set new leakage targets every year. They will be based on company leakage forecasts but will be adjusted if necessary to "ensure adequate progress".

OFWAT also wants parallel progress on work to establish the economic level of leakage for each company in preparation for the 1999 Periodic Review and beyond. This work needs to take into account environmental constraints. This will play an important part in setting forward targets.
"We will be working closely with the Environment Agency, the Department of the Environment and the Welsh Office in setting future targets and will discuss our proposals with them," Byatt added.
OFWAT's statement comes as UK water industry chiefs meet today with deputy Prime Minister John Prescott at an emergency conference to tackle the worst drought the country has faced in 200 years.
